draft.title: Pollution
card: Pollution is the release of harmful substances into air, water or soil. Many of these substances come from human activities.
Air can be polluted by smoke and exhaust gases from burning fuels. Water can be polluted by plastic rubbish and by fertiliser washed off farms into rivers.
Fertiliser in a river can feed algae so they grow fast. When the algae die and rot, they use up oxygen in the water, and fish may die.
Pollution can harm living things and people's health. Breathing polluted air can affect the lungs, and animals can be hurt by eating or becoming tangled in plastic.
draft.remember: Pollution is harmful substances in air, water or soil, often from human activities, and it can harm living things and health.

a.q: Which situation is an example of water pollution caused by human activity?
opts: Fertiliser from a farm washes into a nearby creek
Rain fills a creek after a storm in the hills
Leaves from gum trees fall into a creek and decay
A creek dries up during a long hot summer
a.why: Fertiliser washed off a farm is a harmful substance that humans add to the water. The other options are natural events and do not add a harmful substance from human activity.
a.clue: Look for a harmful substance added by people.

b.q: A council in Lismore finds that a river has many dead fish and a thick green layer of algae near farms. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Fertiliser fed algae, and rotting algae used up oxygen
Fertiliser was eaten by the fish and poisoned them
Plastic bags washed in and made the algae grow faster
Smoke from the farms fell in and made the algae grow
b.why: Fertiliser feeds algae, and when the algae die and rot they use up oxygen, so fish die. The tempting option about fish eating fertiliser skips this step, and the card does not say fertiliser poisons fish directly.
b.clue: Follow the chain from fertiliser to algae to oxygen.

a.best: Fertiliser from a farm washes into a nearby creek

b.best: Fertiliser fed algae, and rotting algae used up oxygen

a.q: Which situation is an example of water pollution caused by human activity?
opts: Fertiliser from a farm washes into a nearby creek

b.q: A council in Lismore finds that a river has many dead fish and a thick green layer of algae near farms. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Fertiliser fed algae, and rotting algae used up oxygen
Fertiliser fed the fish, and the fish used up the oxygen
The algae made too much oxygen, and it harmed the fish
Fertiliser poisoned the fish, and algae fed on them
